entry.summary: An eVisa (tourism or business) before travel; no visa on arrival for Australians.
entry.max_stay: Up to 90 days, single or multiple entry
entry.pre_arrival: Apply only on the Government of Vietnam's official site; details must match the passport exactly. Print the approval. Digital pre-arrival form within 72 hours at Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Phu Quoc airports. A health declaration may be required.
entry.other: Visa status can't be changed in Vietnam; extensions only before expiry, with 6 months' passport validity.

tourism.detail: Australians are eligible for up to 90 days, single or multiple entry.
tourism.next: Apply directly through the national portal and wait for issuance before travel.

meetings.route: eVisa with accurate business purpose; sponsored DN route where the host prefers
meetings.detail: Meetings and trade discussions can use the published entry system without becoming local service delivery.
meetings.next: State the actual business purpose and carry the invitation.

conference.route: eVisa with summit or conference purpose
conference.detail: The eVisa form includes a conference purpose; passive attendance remains separate from speaker or trainer work.
conference.next: If joining the program, have the organiser activate the short-expert or work route.

unpaid-speaking.route: Qualifying under-90-day expert assignment plus host notice
unpaid-speaking.detail: Active delivery can use the short foreign-worker exemption when the person and assignment meet the manager, executive, expert or technical-worker criteria.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the Vietnamese host confirm the expert classification and notify the authority at least three working days before delivery.

paid-speaking.route: Short-expert exemption when qualified; otherwise LĐ2 plus work permit
paid-speaking.detail: A host can activate a genuine short expert assignment; normal local employment or a non-qualifying service uses the work-permit path.
paid-speaking.next: Put credentials, contract, fee, dates and duties into the host's classification.

book-launch.route: Short-expert or work route for active delivery; Vietnamese publisher or bookshop for retail
book-launch.detail: Rights and publisher meetings can stay in the business lane, while a talk, workshop and sales operation should be split.
book-launch.next: Let a local seller handle stock and receipts, then classify any paid or unpaid appearance.

ai-teaching.route: Under-90-day expert exemption plus host notice; LĐ2/work permit for longer teaching
ai-teaching.detail: Science, technology, innovation and digital-transformation experts also have selective exemption possibilities, and a high-threshold digital-professional route can support up to five years.
ai-teaching.next: Have the university, lab, company or province test the credentials against the current expert criteria.

remote-work.detail: The eVisa provides entry but the official visa list does not expressly create a general overseas-remote-work status.
remote-work.next: Pre-clear immigration, labour and tax treatment if Vietnam becomes a remote-work base.

entrepreneur.route: DN2 for establishment activity; investor code and work exemption follow actual capital
entrepreneur.detail: Investor classes begin at different capital levels; an ownership-based work exemption starts at VND3 billion for qualifying company roles.
entrepreneur.next: Choose negotiation, company establishment, investment amount and operating role as separate decisions.

trade.route: eVisa for trade discussions; DN2 or investor/company structure for operation
trade.detail: Offering services, establishing a commercial presence and treaty activity can use DN2, while market-access rules sit under investment law.
trade.next: Use the initial trip for suppliers and partners, then model commercial presence and work status.

artist.route: Host-selected entry and labour route plus performance approval
artist.detail: A foreign performance can require three layers: entry, labour permission and organiser-obtained cultural approval under Decree 144/2020.
artist.next: Have the Vietnamese promoter coordinate all three layers and classify every venue.

mixed-mission.route: eVisa front door plus one Vietnamese host coordinating expert, work, investment or cultural layers
mixed-mission.detail: Vietnam's 90-day eVisa is flexible for arrival; the host is the switchboard for active delivery.
mixed-mission.next: Send the host one schedule separating attendance, delivery, payment, sales, performance and company activity.

laws.rule: There are strict security and investigative measures to stop drug trafficking. Penalties for all types of drug offences, including those with small amounts of drugs, are severe. Drug offences can attract the death penalty or life in jail. Don't use or carry illegal drugs, including marijuana. Marijuana in any form is illegal. It's a crime to have drugs in your system, and you can also be charged for using drugs, even if it was outside of Vietnam. Never carry parcels or luggage for others. For information about carrying prescription medications into Vietnam, see 'Health'. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Foreigners who want to marry a Vietnamese citizen in Vietnam must get formal approval from the Government of Vietnam's Department of Justice. This must be done in the province where the Vietnamese citizen is registered. You also need a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) if you plan to marry in Vietnam. Apply for a CNI through the: You can also apply for the CNI from DFAT in Australia. Fees apply. The embassy or consulate of Vietnam in Australia needs to authenticate it. Only then will the Department of Justice in Vietnam recognise it. - Getting married
laws.heading: Marriage laws

laws.rule: Increased Australian business activity has resulted in a higher number of commercial disputes in recent years. Get professional legal advice before you enter a contract. If you're involved in a business or civil dispute, authorities could stop you from leaving Vietnam until you resolve the matter.
laws.heading: Business laws

laws.rule: Vietnamese authorities may place an exit ban on certain individuals to prevent them from leaving the country. An exit ban can relate to investigations into: an individual, their family or an employer criminal and civil matters, such as business disputes or motor vehicle accidents working without a valid work permit unpaid financial debts People involved in any of these circumstances can request an exit ban for you. You may not be aware that authorities have placed an exit ban on you until you try to leave Vietnam. Your passport may be taken from you until the case is fully investigated and settled. laws.heading: Exit bans

laws.rule: Disputes over alleged misrepresentation of working and living conditions for Australians working in Vietnam often happen. This is especially the case for people teaching English. Before signing an employment contract or travelling to Vietnam for work, verify the true nature of the work you're offered. Check for unacceptable employment conditions. For example, conditions for early termination may state that you surrender your right to a return air ticket. Your potential employer may also withhold your pay. To safeguard your stay, also: check the living arrangements your potential employer has offered make sure you have the correct visa before arriving, ask an embassy or consulate of Vietnam g
laws.heading: Employment

laws.rule: Penalties for serious crime, such as rape, espionage and hijacking, may include the death penalty. It's illegal to: take photos at border crossings or military installations go too close to the border with China, Cambodia or Laos without prior written permission from local authorities gamble, except in government-licensed casinos where foreign passport holders can gamble possess pornography possess non-state sanctioned political or religious material bring, sell, use or distribute electronic cigarettes, vaping devices and vaping liquids These activities may result in arrest and imprisonment. Taking part in unsanctioned religious activities, including online, is against the law. Any involveme
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Some addictive and psychotropic medications are controlled in Vietnam. If you plan to bring medication with you, check if it's legal in Vietnam. Always carry medication in its original packaging. If you're travelling with prescription medication, check the value and quantity restrictions on the import and export of prescription medication with the nearest embassy or consulate of Vietnam.
laws.heading: Medication

laws.rule: You're not allowed to drive or ride on an Australian licence or International Driving Permit (IDP) issued in Australia. Drivers and motorcyclists must have a valid Vietnamese driver licence to drive or ride in Vietnam, including for motorcycles of 50cc or more. Australian citizens can only drive or ride a motorcycle in Vietnam if they hold a temporary Vietnamese driver licence. laws.heading: Driving permit

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Same-sex relationships are legal. However, social and cultural attitudes towards same-sex relationships can be conservative, especially in rural areas. Avoid public displays of affection. Same-sex partners aren't legally protected or recognised. - Advice for LGBTQIA+ travellers

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency of Vietnam is the Vietnamese Dong (VND). When you arrive or exit Vietnam, declare: foreign currency in excess of $US5,000, including cash and traveller's cheques more than 15 million Vietnamese dong If you carry more currency or gold than you declared, authorities could confiscate it. They could arrest or fine you. These requirements may be subject to change. Contact the nearest embassy or consulate of Vietnam for details. Credit cards are widely accepted throughout major cities in Vietnam. ATMs are widespread in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Da Nang. Check with your bank to confirm
